piece: W1-19 — the main quest, end to end
corpus_item: RI-QST06 §B Act IV — The Voices. Eight quests, stakes 8-9, ALL open simultaneously off the Act III closer, >=4 with a resolution gated on requires.faction_rank, mean resolutions >= 3.0, and no rank_gate anywhere because rank is leverage and never a wall.
note: Every quest here declares prerequisite_quests: ['Q-MAIN-15'] and nothing else. No Act IV quest is sequenced behind another Act IV quest; the act is a campaign the player sequences, which is the whole point of RI-QST06's simultaneity check. Every one of the eight is completable by a player who joined nothing, at a price in gold, evidence or reputation.

quests.title: The Sexton's Voice

giver.location: Soulrest, the Drowned Court's chapter room behind the counting house

quests.directions: The chapter sits in the long room behind the counting house on the burial stair at Soulrest, once a season, and the whole Court comes in for it from Lilmoth and Gideon and the coast houses. Nine sextons vote and Rell is one of them. The other eight keep rooms along the stair for the week of it and every one of them can be found and talked to before the doors shut.

journal.text: The Court will not open its own crypt road to a machine it has not voted on. Nine sextons, and I need five of them, and Rell has one vote and a great deal of opinion about the other eight.

Four are Rell's already. Two will not move for anything I have. The three in the middle are a Lilmoth sexton who wants the Court out of Lilmoth, an old woman who has read the Recension in four copies and believes none of them, and a man who is in debt to the Wet Ledger for eleven hundred.

The old woman asked me one question, which was whether I thought the ninth clause was written for me. I said I did not know. She said that was the first honest answer she had had out of anyone in the chapter room in thirty years and voted with me.

The man in debt can be bought, which costs eleven hundred, or his debt can be read out, which ruins him and gets his vote and loses me the two who were never going to move plus one who was. Rell would prefer I bought him. Rell would prefer a great many things she has not said out loud.
The chapter voted four to five against and the crypt road is shut behind the third gate by the Court's own order. There are other ways down and none of them are the Court's.

Five of nine. The Court stands with me and the crypt road is open to the gallery for as long as this chapter sits. Rell counted the hands twice and then went and stood by the water marks on the wall for a while.

I read the sexton's debt out in front of the chapter and got him and lost two others, and it came to five anyway. He resigned in the morning. Rell has the vote she wanted and a Court that is going to be difficult about it for a decade.

The Court stands with me because I am a sexton of it now, in the ninth chair, which they gave me rather than argue about whether an outlander may be counted. It is a chair with no work attached and a vote attached, and everyone in that room knows exactly what it cost them.

I paid eleven hundred of my own gold to settle a sexton's debt to the Wet Ledger and he voted as he said he would. None was ruined and none was persuaded and I am poorer, and that is a way of winning a vote.

branches.condition: The player chooses how to reach the indebted sexton: pay it, expose it, or go round him on rank
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: Five of nine, argued. The Court opens the crypt road and the chapter stays whole.
Five of nine, at the cost of a sexton's career and the chapter's temper. The Court opens the road and will be arguing about it for ten years.
The Court seats the player in the ninth chair rather than debate whether an outlander may be counted, and the vote follows the chair. Available only to somebody the Court already ranks.
Eleven hundred gold settles a sexton's debt and buys his vote without ruining him. The most expensive route and the one that closes nothing.

failure_states.cause: The chapter closes its doors with fewer than five votes
failure_states.consequence: The Court's road is shut behind the third gate. The gallery must be reached from the Bone Ladder shaft or from below with the skei, and the Act V approach is longer and unlit.

deceit.stated_objective: Win the Court's chapter to the opening of the Count
deceit.actual_objective: Win the Court's chapter to the opening of the Count, and settle who runs the Court afterwards
deceit.truth: Rell is not counting five votes for the machine. She is counting five votes for herself, and the tally-reader is the instrument she is counting them with.

rewards.name: the crypt road, open to the gallery
the old woman who has read the Recension in four copies
what the Ledger holds over the Court
a room on the burial stair for the week of the chapter
what eleven hundred buys in the Court

quests.notes: Act IV voice 1 of 8. Four resolutions, one rank-gated, one gold-gated, none violent.

quests.title: The Ledger's Voice

giver.location: Gideon, the counting floor over the toll gate at the market cross
giver.disposition_min_note: W1-19 round 2 re-clamp. Round 1 set every clamped gate to the WORST signature's COLD-START standing at this giver, measured by an offer-gate probe that only ever looks at frame zero. That left all nine clamped gates with a worst-case margin of exactly 0, and the piece's own first quest then moved the derived faction term by -12, so eleven of forty signatures could not finish and the main quest closed itself twenty-two quests later. This number is set from `tools/quests/mainline-chain-floor.mjs`, which measures the standing at this giver at EVERY STEP of both chains for all forty signatures, with consequences accumulating and no topic hand-fed. The rule: a gate keeps its rank order and its race discrimination, and sits far enough below the measured chain floor that the shortfall left is one a purse can close (RI-DLG04 §C, seam S15). Availability is never a function of birth; price is.

quests.directions: Ruvela Sath keeps the counting floor over the toll gate at Gideon's market cross, above where Belliene used to sit. The Ledger's compact meets in the warehouse behind it, the long one with the double doors on the river side, and it meets whenever eleven of the nineteen factors are in Gideon, which is most weeks in the dry season and never in the wet.

journal.text: The Wet Ledger owns the river freight and every barge that could carry what will have to come out of the Stone Wastes. Ruvela Sath will put it to the compact for me and she has been clear that the compact does not vote on theology and will not be asked to.

Their objection is not superstition and I was wrong to expect it to be. Eleven of the nineteen have money in gem freight out of Archon. If the province decides the gem trade is what killed the tide, they are ruined, and they would rather it were the Cutters or the machine or anything at all.

It is convenient, because it is not the gem trade, and I can prove it. The tonnage out of Archon is five times what it was and it is nothing against four hundred years of return column. I came in expecting to fight these people and what I actually have is the only exoneration they are ever going to get.

Sath wants the exoneration and does not want it read out with the true tonnage attached, because the true tonnage is a crime even if it is not the crime. Either the compact hears the whole arithmetic or it hears the half that helps it, and the half that helps it is a lie that happens to be true. She put it to me as a courtesy and it was not one.
The compact declined to meet and Sath has stopped answering. The river freight is closed to whatever comes out of the Wastes and there are no other barges in this province.

I read the whole arithmetic to eleven factors in a warehouse — the return column, the tonnage, the dates, all of it. They are exonerated of the thing that matters and indicted for the thing that does not, and they voted with me anyway because the arithmetic was in the Court's own hand with Hosk-Vei's name under mine.
I gave the compact the half that helped them and kept the tonnage back. They voted with me in an afternoon. Sath shook my hand and I have written down here that I knew what I was doing.

The compact voted with me because I hold a name in it and asked for it as a Ledger matter rather than a provincial one. Sath had to spend a favour to make that work and she has told me the size of the favour twice.

Two thousand gold, paid to the compact as a surety against the freight, and the vote came with it. The Ledger does not consider this a bribe. The Ledger considers this how business is done and is correct that the two are hard to tell apart.

branches.condition: The player decides whether the compact hears the whole arithmetic or only the part that exonerates it
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The compact hears everything and votes with the player anyway. The gem trade is on the record as a crime; the Blackwood Company thread stays live into Act V and the Ledger's own factors are exposed to the Assize.
The compact hears the exoneration without the tonnage. The vote is quick, the gem trade goes on unindicted, and the Dockhands who load it lose the only chance anyone was going to give them.
The compact treats it as Ledger business because the player is Ledger. Fastest route, and Sath spends a favour that she will ask back in Act V.
resolutions.joins_faction_note: W1-19 round 2. This resolution is named `..._rank`: the player TAKES THE RANK. Until now that granted reputation and nothing else, and `sim.quest.factions[f].member` was set true by nothing in the build, so RI-DLG04 §B's faction term — the one thing `race-reactions.json` §repair_paths names as the route through a -40 race row — had no world-side way to fire at all. Joining is a declared act and it is allowed to cost you with the rivals; that is the design in `faction-reactions.json §application`, and it is why the ordinary route through this quest does not join and this one does.

resolutions.outcome: Two thousand gold as a surety against the freight buys the vote outright. Open to a player with no standing anywhere, which is the point.

failure_states.cause: The compact does not meet before the wet season closes the river
failure_states.consequence: River freight is closed until the dry season. The Act V approach must be provisioned overland from Bone Ladder, which is slower and which the Assize watches.

deceit.stated_objective: Persuade the Ledger's compact to carry what comes out of the Stone Wastes
deceit.actual_objective: Obtain from a stranger an exoneration of the gem trade that the Ledger can quote afterwards
deceit.truth: Eleven of the nineteen factors have money in gem freight. The arithmetic that clears them of killing the tide also proves they are running five times the tonnage they declare, and Sath wants the first half of that sentence in the minutes and the second half nowhere.

rewards.name: an Assize that has the gem trade on the record
the size of the favour, stated twice
a surety lodged against the freight

quests.notes: Act IV voice 2 of 8. The leverage act at its clearest: the same true arithmetic is an exoneration and an indictment, and the player chooses how much of it the room hears.

quests.title: The Deep-Kin's Voice

giver.location: Helstrom, the root gallery under the eastern terrace
giver.disposition_min_note: W1-19 round 2 re-clamp. Round 1 set every clamped gate to the WORST signature's COLD-START standing at this giver, measured by an offer-gate probe that only ever looks at frame zero. That left all nine clamped gates with a worst-case margin of exactly 0, and the piece's own first quest then moved the derived faction term by -12, so eleven of forty signatures could not finish and the main quest closed itself twenty-two quests later. quests.directions: Back to the root gallery under the eastern terrace at Helstrom, through the cistern arch and left at the water noise. The Deep-Kin do not vote and there is nothing to attend. What there is, is eleven rootkeepers who between them speak for the interior, and they are not in Helstrom; they are at eleven wells, and Ashul-Tei will name them and their wells and will not carry a word for you.

journal.text: The Deep-Kin do not have a vote to win. They have eleven rootkeepers at eleven wells and a consensus that forms when enough of them stop objecting, and Ashul-Tei says that if I want it I will have to walk to them, all of them, and that she will not send ahead.

Seven of the eleven will not object if the interior is not opened to Court traffic. Two object to me personally, being an outlander with a Court name. Two object to the whole idea on the grounds that a foreigner reading the Count is exactly what the Court would want them to believe is prophecy.

The two who object to the idea are not wrong and I did not try to tell them they were. I gave them Bel Mourne's copies with the gap in them and let them read the Court's own argument against its own text.

The last two want a price and the price is not gold. They want the crypt road sealed behind me when it is done, so that whatever is under the Wastes stays a thing the Court has to walk two days to reach. That is a promise I can make and would then have to keep in the last hour of this. Four ways to a consensus that does not object, and each one closes the rest: an interior told the fourth sentence cannot then be walked to over nineteen days, and a keeper's name spent is spent.
The consensus did not form. Four keepers still object and the interior will not have me at any well east of the Rootlands, which is most of the wells between here and the Wastes.

There is no objection any more. I walked to eleven wells in nineteen days and gave two of them the Court's own doubt to read and promised two of them the road would be sealed after, and the interior has stopped objecting, which is the only kind of yes it gives.

I told the eleven what the tree at Thorn said, all four sentences of it, and the consensus formed in a day and it formed as fury. I got what I came for and Sesh-Anaat asked me not to do this and I did it, and the interior is going to do something about the coast that no plan of mine covers.

Sesh-Anaat's keeper-name got me heard at every well without an argument. Eleven keepers, nineteen days of walking, and not one of them asked me who I was, because a voice they trust had already answered that.

I put it to the eleven as one of them, because I am one of them, and it stopped being a question about an outlander and became a question about what the interior does next. It took four days. I was not thanked and was not supposed to be.

branches.condition: The player may repeat the tree's fourth sentence to the eleven keepers, which forms the consensus at once and out of fury
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The consensus forms over nineteen days of walking, at the price of a promise to seal the crypt road afterwards. The promise is checked in Act V and breaking it costs the interior's standing in the final hour.

The consensus forms in a day, as fury, because the player told eleven rootkeepers that the Hist does not know what to do. The interior mobilises against the coast on its own account and the Rootkeepers and Sesh-Anaat are lost for the rest of the game.
Sesh-Anaat's keeper-name opens every well without argument. The cheapest route and it requires having kept the fourth sentence in Q-MAIN-15.
A player counted among the Xul-Aneekh puts it to the eleven as one of them, and the consensus forms because the question is internal.
resolutions.joins_faction_note: W1-19 round 2. This resolution is named `..._rank`: the player TAKES THE RANK. Until now that granted reputation and nothing else, and `sim.quest.factions[f].member` was set true by nothing in the build, so RI-DLG04 §B's faction term — the one thing `race-reactions.json` §repair_paths names as the route through a -40 race row — had no world-side way to fire at all. Joining is a declared act and it is allowed to cost you with the rivals; that is the design in `faction-reactions.json §application`, and it is why the ordinary route through this quest does not join and this one does.

failure_states.cause: Four or more keepers still object when the player leaves the interior
failure_states.consequence: No well east of the Rootlands will take the player. The Act V approach must be made without resting in the interior, and the Deep-Kin will stand with the antagonist in the last hour.

deceit.stated_objective: Obtain the interior's consent to the opening of the Count
deceit.actual_objective: Obtain the interior's consent to the opening of the Count
deceit.truth: Two of the eleven believe the tally-reader is exactly what a Court that needed a claimant would produce, and nothing in this quest or any other proves them wrong. The fastest way to the consensus is to tell them the Hist has no instruction, which is true, which the keeper of Thorn asked the player not to do, and which sets the interior moving on its own.

rewards.name: what the interior will do about the coast
the interior, in a day, as fury

quests.notes: Act IV voice 3 of 8. Nineteen days of walking is the honest route; the fast route spends a secret the player was asked to keep and changes the world for the rest of the game.

quests.title: The Cutters' Voice

giver.location: Blackrose, the cutting yard behind the reed-walk
giver.disposition_min_note: W1-19 round 2 re-clamp. quests.directions: The cutting yard behind the reed-walk at Blackrose, and after that the three other yards, which are at Mudwater Landing, at Salt-Egg Camp and at the far end of the Lilmoth wharf where nobody admits there is one. The cutters at the fourth yard will not talk to anyone Neeja-Xul sends, so if you want them you go without her name on you.

journal.text: The intakes cannot be reached from below without cutters. Eleven live roots, all of them in water, and there are four yards in this province that know how to open one without killing it. Neeja-Xul speaks for one of them. I have four yards to find and one season to do it in.

Mudwater and Salt-Egg will come if Blackrose comes. The fourth yard is at Lilmoth and it is not a yard, it is two brothers and a Blackwood Company retainer, and they have been paid a year in advance for something they will not describe. I went to the fourth yard without her name on me, as she told me to.

The Company has bought the Lilmoth cutters to be ready to cut on its own account, which only makes sense if the Company has been told what is under the Wastes. It has been. There are five people who could have and I have been talking to all of them. The Lilmoth yard is shown to the others as bought, or bought back quietly, or gone round entirely on my own standing — never two of those, because the first makes the second pointless and the third makes both unnecessary. Whichever of the three I take closes the other two, and none of them can be tried after another has failed.
The yards will not come. Blackrose will not move without Lilmoth and Lilmoth is bought, and the roots below the Wastes will have to be cut by hands that do not know how, or not at all.

Three yards, and the fourth stood down when I put the Company's retainer in front of the other three and let them look at him. Cutters are not sentimental about each other and they are extremely sentimental about being sold.
I bought the Lilmoth yard out from under the Company for eighteen hundred, which is more than the Company paid and less than the Company will pay to find out who did it. All four yards will come.

The yards came because I am one of them now, in the way the Ixtu-Vakh count it, which is that I have cut a well and it is on the list. Neeja-Xul read my name out at the yard and there was no argument, and I noticed that not one of them looked at me either.

branches.condition: The player deals with the bought Lilmoth yard: expose it, outbid it, or stand on their own standing among the Cutters
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The Lilmoth yard is shown to the other three as bought. It stands down, the Company loses its cutters, and the Company learns who did that to it.
Eighteen hundred gold takes the Lilmoth yard off the Company quietly. All four yards come and the Company does not know why until Act V.
A player on the Cutters' own list gets the yards by asking. Requires having cut a well without leave, which is a crime in the interior and a qualification here.
resolutions.joins_faction_note: W1-19 round 2. This resolution is named `..._rank`: the player TAKES THE RANK. Joining is a declared act and it is allowed to cost you with the rivals; that is the design in `faction-reactions.json §application`, and it is why the ordinary route through this quest does not join and this one does.

failure_states.cause: Blackrose will not move while the Lilmoth yard is bought
failure_states.consequence: No cutters. The eleven live roots below the Wastes cannot be opened from below at all, which closes the backpath's route through Q-MAIN-31 and forces Act V through the Court's gallery.

deceit.stated_objective: Get the four cutting yards to come to the Stone Wastes
deceit.actual_objective: Get the four cutting yards to come to the Stone Wastes
deceit.truth: The Blackwood Company has already bought the Lilmoth yard, a year in advance, to cut on its own account. Somebody who knows what is under the Wastes sold that knowledge, and the quest does not establish which of the five candidates it was.

rewards.name: somebody sold the Company what is under the Wastes
a name on the Cutters’ list

quests.notes: Act IV voice 4 of 8. Who told the Blackwood Company is one of the five declared unanswered questions; the Act V conversation raises it and does not close it.

quests.title: The Assize's Voice

giver.location: Stormhold, the walled quarter above the cistern
giver.disposition_min_note: W1-19 round 2 re-clamp. Round 1 set every clamped gate to the WORST signature's COLD-START standing at this giver, measured by an offer-gate probe that only ever looks at frame zero. That left all nine clamped gates with a worst-case margin of exactly 0, and the piece's own first quest then moved the derived faction term by -12, so eleven of forty signatures could not finish and the main quest closed itself twenty-two quests later. This number is set from `tools/quests/mainline-chain-floor.mjs`, which measures the standing at this giver at EVERY STEP of both chains for all forty signatures, with consequences accumulating and no topic hand-fed. The rule: a gate keeps its rank order and its race discrimination, and sits far enough below the measured chain floor that the shortfall left is one a purse can close (RI-DLG04 §C, seam S15). Availability is never a function of birth; price is.

quests.directions: Stormhold's walled quarter is up the hill from the cistern, behind the only gate in the province that is shut at night for a reason that is not water. Prefect Galvus Arn sits in the writ-house at the top of it. What is needed from him is a writ of works, which is the paper that makes an excavation under the Stone Wastes lawful, and without which every cutter and barge involved is committing a crime the Assize will eventually get round to.

journal.text: The Prefect can issue a writ of works. Without it the whole business is an unlicensed excavation on Imperial-chartered ground and everyone who lifts a stone for me is liable. He has not said no. He has said what a writ of works normally requires and it is a list of four things I do not have.

What he wants is not on the list. Stormhold has two cohorts on paper and one in fact, because the reserves went to Vvardenfell, and the Prefect has been writing to the Governor at Gideon about it for two years. He wants the province's other powers on a piece of paper agreeing that the Empire is needed for something. He told me this himself, once I stopped pretending not to have noticed.

So the writ is not about the machine. The writ is a lever he is using me to pull on a governor ninety leagues of bad road away. He was completely open about it once I stopped pretending not to have noticed, and he is not ashamed of it, and it is still the cheapest thing I have been asked for in this whole act.

No writ. The Assize has instead posted a notice that any excavation under the Stone Wastes is unlawful and that the Court's crypt road is Imperial ground, which it is not, and which is not going to be tested in Soulrest.

The writ of works is signed and sealed and it cost me nothing but a paragraph, which the Prefect wrote himself and I put my name to, saying that the province's powers have asked the Empire for its help. He will send it to Gideon by the fast boat.

I put the Court's arithmetic in front of the Assize as evidence in the ordinary way and got the writ as a finding of fact rather than a favour. It took six weeks and three clerks and it is the only piece of paper in this whole business that would survive being read out by an enemy.

The writ came through the Assize's own hand because I am sworn to it, which took a morning. The Prefect did not need the paragraph after all and asked for it anyway and I gave it to him, and I am not sure which of us that was a favour to.

branches.condition: The player gives the Prefect his paragraph, forces the writ as a finding of fact on the evidence, or takes it on Assize standing
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The writ is issued in exchange for a signed sentence the Prefect will use against his own Governor. Cheap, fast, and it puts the player's name on an Imperial political document that will be read in Cyrodiil.
The writ is issued on the evidence, as a finding. Slowest route, no political debt, and the only document in Act IV that stands up in Act V when somebody challenges the player's standing.
A sworn player gets the writ in a morning through the Assize's own hand.
resolutions.joins_faction_note: W1-19 round 2. This resolution is named `..._rank`: the player TAKES THE RANK. Until now that granted reputation and nothing else, and `sim.quest.factions[f].member` was set true by nothing in the build, so RI-DLG04 §B's faction term — the one thing `race-reactions.json` §repair_paths names as the route through a -40 race row — had no world-side way to fire at all. Joining is a declared act and it is allowed to cost you with the rivals; that is the design in `faction-reactions.json §application`, and it is why the ordinary route through this quest does not join and this one does.

failure_states.cause: The Prefect refuses and posts a notice instead
failure_states.consequence: The excavation is unlawful. Every Act V approach that uses barges or cutters accrues a bounty, and the Assize will be waiting at the top of the stair in the aftermath.

deceit.stated_objective: Obtain a writ of works for an excavation under the Stone Wastes
deceit.actual_objective: Obtain from the province's powers a written admission that the Empire is needed, to be sent to a Governor who has not left his compound in two years
deceit.truth: The Prefect does not care what is under the Stone Wastes. He has one cohort where he is owed two and he has been writing about it for two years, and a stranger who needs a signature is the first lever he has been handed.

rewards.name: the cohorts Stormhold does not have
what a paragraph is worth to a Prefect
sworn to the Assize, and it shows

quests.notes: Act IV voice 5 of 8. D4: the Prefect's price is lawful, legitimate, and uses the player as an instrument in someone else's argument; refusing it is not a failure state, it is res_finding_of_fact, which costs eleven days instead.

quests.title: The Wharf's Voice

giver.location: Lilmoth, the third mooring at the head of the wharf
giver.disposition_min_note: W1-19 round 2 re-clamp. Round 1 set every clamped gate to the WORST signature's COLD-START standing at this giver, measured by an offer-gate probe that only ever looks at frame zero. That left all nine clamped gates with a worst-case margin of exactly 0, and the piece's own first quest then moved the derived faction term by -12, so eleven of forty signatures could not finish and the main quest closed itself twenty-two quests later. This number is set from `tools/quests/mainline-chain-floor.mjs`, which measures the standing at this giver at EVERY STEP of both chains for all forty signatures, with consequences accumulating and no topic hand-fed. The rule: a gate keeps its rank order and its race discrimination, and sits far enough below the measured chain floor that the shortfall left is one a purse can close (RI-DLG04 §C, seam S15). Availability is never a function of birth; price is.

quests.directions: Lilmoth is at the far south where the Rootlands go into the sea, and the wharf is most of the city that still works. The third mooring is at the head of it and the hiring happens there at first light. Weeja-Sen does the hiring. The rotting quarter is behind the wharf and nobody goes in and that is where the Company keeps its people, which is not a secret, it is just not said on the wharf.

journal.text: Whatever comes out of the Wastes has to be carried by hands, and the hands in this province are on Weeja-Sen's list at Lilmoth. She will hire out sixty for the work. She wants to know what the work is and she has already been told a version of it by another. She wants to know what the work is and I have to decide how much of it to tell her.

The Blackwood Company got here first. Their factor has offered her list double for the same season and will not say what for, and she has not taken it, and she has not refused it either, and she is doing that on purpose in front of me.

Her price is not gold and she said so straight away. Eleven of her people went into the rotting quarter over the last two winters on Company hire and did not come out, and Lilmoth will not go in after them because there is a Hist in there and its rootkeepers do not acknowledge that the Empire exists, let alone a dockmaster. She told me the price and then waited to see whether I would ask what was in the quarter.

So the wharf's voice costs a walk into the rotting quarter to find out what happened to eleven people. I can do that, or I can outbid a trading company with more money than the province, or I can hire the list as a Dockhand and let the list decide for itself, which it will do badly and in my favour. Weeja-Sen asked for eleven names. If I answer with coin instead she takes the coin, and she does not ask again, and the eleven stay where they are for good. Answering her with coin closes the naming, and answering with names closes the buying, and neither is offered twice.

The Company took the list. Sixty hands are working the rotting quarter this season for a buyer who will not say what for, and I have thirty of the wrong sort out of Gideon at twice the price and half the use.

Eleven names, and I brought back what happened to nine of them, which is that the Company had them cutting inside the rotting quarter and the rootkeepers in there stopped them the way rootkeepers do. Weeja-Sen read the nine names out on the wharf at first light and the list is mine and the Company will not hire in Lilmoth again this year.

I paid over the Company's offer out of my own purse and the list came with it. Weeja-Sen took the money and she has not looked at me the same way since, because she asked me for eleven names and I gave her coin.

I am on the list myself and the list hires the list, so I asked at first light like anyone else and sixty came. Weeja-Sen says this is not a favour, it is how the wharf works, and that I should stop thanking her for it.

branches.condition: The player goes into the rotting quarter for the eleven, outbids the Company, or hires the list from inside it
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: Nine of the eleven are accounted for and read out on the wharf. The Company is shut out of Lilmoth hiring for the year, the rotting quarter's rootkeepers know the player's face, and the wharf's voice is given rather than sold.
The list is bought over the Company's head for two thousand four hundred. Weeja-Sen keeps her eleven unaccounted for and remembers that she asked for names and was given coin.
A player on the hiring list hires from the hiring list. Costs nothing and leaves the eleven where they are.
resolutions.joins_faction_note: W1-19 round 2. This resolution is named `..._rank`: the player TAKES THE RANK. Until now that granted reputation and nothing else, and `sim.quest.factions[f].member` was set true by nothing in the build, so RI-DLG04 §B's faction term — the one thing `race-reactions.json` §repair_paths names as the route through a -40 race row — had no world-side way to fire at all. Joining is a declared act and it is allowed to cost you with the rivals; that is the design in `faction-reactions.json §application`, and it is why the ordinary route through this quest does not join and this one does.

failure_states.cause: The Company's offer stands unanswered when the season's hiring closes
failure_states.consequence: Sixty hands work for the Blackwood Company instead. The Act V approach is undermanned, the Company is inside the Stone Wastes ahead of the player, and one Act V topic opens that does not otherwise exist.

deceit.stated_objective: Hire sixty hands off the Lilmoth list
deceit.actual_objective: Hire sixty hands off the Lilmoth list
deceit.truth: The Blackwood Company has been hiring the same list for two winters to cut inside the rotting quarter, and eleven of the people it hired did not come back. Two of the eleven are not accounted for by anything in this game.

rewards.name: sixty hands off the Lilmoth list
the eleven who went into the rotting quarter
Weeja-Sen, who asked for names and got them
the hiring list for a season
a place on the hiring list

quests.notes: Act IV voice 6 of 8. Two of the eleven are never accounted for anywhere in the game and no sealed answer will be written for them by this piece; they are registered in mainline.json as a declared silence.

quests.title: The Rootkeepers' Voice

giver.location: Thorn, the sapwell at the foot of the causeway
giver.disposition_min_note: W1-19 round 2 re-clamp. Round 1 set every clamped gate to the WORST signature's COLD-START standing at this giver, measured by an offer-gate probe that only ever looks at frame zero. That left all nine clamped gates with a worst-case margin of exactly 0, and the piece's own first quest then moved the derived faction term by -12, so eleven of forty signatures could not finish and the main quest closed itself twenty-two quests later. This number is set from `tools/quests/mainline-chain-floor.mjs`, which measures the standing at this giver at EVERY STEP of both chains for all forty signatures, with consequences accumulating and no topic hand-fed. The rule: a gate keeps its rank order and its race discrimination, and sits far enough below the measured chain floor that the shortfall left is one a purse can close (RI-DLG04 §C, seam S15). Availability is never a function of birth; price is.

quests.directions: Sesh-Anaat is at the well at the foot of the causeway at Thorn, at low water, as before. What she is being asked for is leave to open eleven live roots, which is the thing her whole order exists to prevent, and she will hear it standing in the water and not indoors.

journal.text: Eleven live roots have to be opened to reach the intakes from below and only the rootkeepers can give leave for that. What I am asking Sesh-Anaat for is the thing her order exists to refuse. She heard the whole of it without interrupting and then stood in the water for a long time.

The keepers' answer is a rite and not a vote. Leave to open a live root is given by three keepers standing at the root, and it has been given eleven times in four hundred years, and every one of the eleven is written down with the reason and whether the reason held. She read me the rite before she would hear what I wanted it for.

She read me the eleven. Nine of them were for water. One was for a road. One was in the year the Knahaten Flu came out of Stormhold and it is the only one where the reason is written as: we did not know what else to do.

She will stand for it herself and she needs two more keepers and the two nearest are the ones who will ask what the tree at Thorn told me. If I answer that honestly the leave will not be given by anyone. If I do not answer it, the leave is given on a silence, and the silence will be in the book next to my name for four hundred years. The leave is given on the true reason, on a silence, or on a technicality, and whichever it is goes into the book in ink and is read by keepers for four hundred years. There is no second asking. Each of the three closes the other two the moment it is written in the book, and the book is never again opened at that page.
Leave was not given. The roots stay shut, the intakes cannot be reached from below, and everything now has to go through the Court's gallery and the Court's chapter and the Court's terms.

Three keepers stood at the root at Thorn and gave leave for eleven, and the reason written in the book is the true one, which is that the wells are drinking an allowance and what happens when it stops is not known. Sesh-Anaat wrote it in her own hand and put my name under hers.

The leave was given and I did not answer the question I was asked. It is written as given on a silence. Sesh-Anaat knows exactly what I did not say and gave it anyway, and I do not know whether that was trust or whether she was as frightened as I was.

Leave was given because I asked for it as a keeper of a well, which I am, having cut one, in a way the order does not recognise and the book does. There is a list of everyone who has ever done that and the list is short and every other name on it is followed by a note about how they died.

branches.condition: The player answers the two keepers' question about the tree honestly and loses the leave, declines to answer and receives it on a silence, or claims it as a well-cutter
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: Leave for eleven roots, given openly, with the true reason in the book. Requires that the player never spoke the tree's fourth sentence and can therefore answer the keepers' question without lying.
Leave given on a silence. The player declines to answer and it is written down that they declined, for four hundred years, next to their name.
Leave claimed as somebody who has cut a well, which the order does not recognise and its own book does. Requires having cut the Bone Ladder well open in Q-MAIN-03 or taken the skei.

failure_states.cause: Fewer than three keepers will stand at the root
failure_states.consequence: The eleven roots stay shut. Everything must go through the Court's gallery, which makes the Court's voice a hard requirement instead of one of eight, and closes the backpath's cut route.

deceit.stated_objective: Obtain the rootkeepers' leave to open eleven live roots
deceit.actual_objective: Obtain the rootkeepers' leave to open eleven live roots
deceit.truth: Leave has been given eleven times in four hundred years and the book records whether the reason held. In one of the eleven the reason is written as: we did not know what else to do. The player's is the twelfth.

rewards.name: the twelfth leave, written in her hand
what a silence costs in four hundred years
how the other names on that list died

quests.notes: Act IV voice 7 of 8. The only voice whose price is a truth rather than a resource, and the only one where refusing to answer is itself a resolution with a permanent record.

quests.title: The Salt Voice

giver.location: Archon, the Dres factor-house behind the stone quay
giver.disposition_min_note: W1-19 round 2 re-clamp, SET FROM THE MEASURED ARRIVAL. Round 1 set every clamped gate to the WORST signature's COLD-START standing at this giver, measured by an offer-gate probe that only ever looks at frame zero. That left all nine clamped gates with a worst-case margin of exactly 0, and the piece's own first quest then moved the derived faction term by -12, so eleven of forty signatures could not finish and the main quest closed itself twenty-two quests later. The round-2 pass then set this to 12 from `chain_floor` — the minimum standing at ANY step of the chain — and 12 was still wrong in the other direction: it left the four Saxhleel signatures 1.96 points short at the moment they actually walk up to this door, and they finished only by paying a 1000-drake bribe. THIS number comes from `arrival_floor` in `tools/quests/mainline-chain-floor.mjs --sabotage no-purse`: the standing the WORST signature arrives with, having played the whole intended chain with consequences accumulating, no topic hand-fed, and no money at all. Measured worst arrival: 10.04 (all four saxhleel signatures; naga 14.04, khajiit 34.04, dunmer up to 58.40). Clamped to 8, leaving a reserve of 2.04 that a route the trace did not take can spend. A gate has to be passable at the instant you reach it, not at every instant of the game — `chain_floor` prices doors nothing is short at, and a cold-start clamp prices nothing at all. NOTE, because the earlier draft of this note overclaimed: `disposition_min_race_blind` is a PROVENANCE RECORD of the pre-clamp authored value and is read by no engine code. The race discrimination is not in this number and never was — it is in the standing itself, where a Saxhleel stands thirty points below an Imperial at a House Dres factor's table, which is the design and is untouched. What changed is that being short is now priced (RI-DLG04 §C, seam S15) instead of final. Availability is never a function of birth; price is.

quests.directions: The Dres factor-house at Archon is behind the stone quay, the compound with its own water and its own gate, and Neloth Vaun does not come out of it. Getting in is a matter of being expected. Nobody in Archon will take a message in for you and the crane crew will tell you why if you buy them a drink and do not write anything down.

journal.text: The crane crew at Archon say that whatever goes out of the Wastes goes past House Dres, because Dres owns the deep water and the coast road both, and that the factor in the compound behind the quay has already been asked about it by a party who is not me.

Neloth Vaun is the Dres salt-factor at Archon and he holds the deep-water berth. He has heard the whole business already and he does not care about the tide, the Court, the trees or me. He cares that eleven cutters and sixty hands are about to be in one place under Imperial writ, and he wants to know what that does to the price of stock.

He wants a clause. He wants it written into the writ of works that the labour engaged is engaged by contract and is not therefore available for any other purpose, which sounds like nothing and means that sixty free Argonians working under an Imperial writ cannot be taken by a Dres raiding party, and he wants that because a raid on a lawful Imperial works is the one thing that would bring the cohorts back to this province. He put the wording in front of me and waited while I read it twice.

The clause protects sixty people who would otherwise be exactly the stock his House takes. He is asking for it to protect his House's freedom to keep taking everyone else, by keeping the Legion out. It is the best thing anyone has offered me in this act and the reason for it is the worst. The clause is signed or it is not. If I sign it, sixty people are safe for a season and House Dres has its year; if I refuse it and buy the water, the sixty are not safe and Vaun has my name. I cannot have the berth and the refusal both. Signing closes the refusal and refusing closes the signing; I cannot have the berth on both terms and the compound will not pretend otherwise.

Vaun will not open the deep-water berth. Everything that comes out has to go over the bar at Archon in shallow-draught boats, in four times the number of trips, past a coast that House Dres also owns.

The clause is in the writ and the berth is open. Sixty people who would have been stock are, for one season, not, and House Dres has bought itself another year of the Legion staying in Vvardenfell, and I signed that.

I refused the clause and told him what he could do with the berth and then bought the deep water off his own harbourmaster at four times the rate through the Ledger's barges. It cost three thousand and Vaun sent word that he respects it and that he will remember it, and both of those were probably threats.

I told Vaun that the true tonnage out of this quay was in a book with an Assize seal on it and that a raid on the works would put both in front of a Prefect who is looking for a reason to ask for his cohorts back. He opened the berth without the clause. He was not frightened. He did the arithmetic in front of me and it came out the same way.

branches.condition: The player signs the clause, refuses and pays for the water another way, or turns the Assize evidence back on the factor
The player must choose which declared resolution and consequence to accept

resolutions.outcome: The clause is written into the writ. Sixty labourers are protected from Dres raiding for a season and House Dres is protected from the Legion for a year. Both are true and the game does not say which weighs more.
The clause is refused and the deep water is bought through the Ledger at four times the rate. Three thousand gold, no protection for the sixty, and a Dres factor who says he will remember it.

The berth opens without the clause, because the factor does the arithmetic on what a raid would cost him with the Assize already holding Archon's true tonnage. Requires the Archon manifests and the writ both.
resolutions.attribute_scale_note: W1-19 round 2, gen 3. Was `personality: 45`, the highest attribute demand in the build and unreachable by all 240 sheets (ceiling 31). Re-set to 20: two under the ceiling a MEDIAN sheet reaches by carrying mercantile and speechcraft to 100, and above the 18 a bottom-decile sheet can reach, so this stays the hardest social check on the spine — Q-MAIN-08's is 17 — and a character who did not build for it still has res_sign_the_clause and res_buy_the_water. Clamping to the ceiling itself (31, one sheet in 240) would have been the same defect one point lower; the reserve is deliberate, per the round-1 finding that nine gates clamped with a margin of exactly zero.

failure_states.cause: The factor closes the deep-water berth to the works
failure_states.consequence: Four times the trips over the Archon bar in shallow boats along a coast House Dres owns. The Act V approach is delayed and the Company reaches the Wastes first.

deceit.stated_objective: Open the deep-water berth at Archon to the works
deceit.actual_objective: Obtain, from somebody with an Imperial writ, a clause that keeps the Legion out of Black Marsh for another year
deceit.truth: The clause genuinely protects sixty free Argonians from being taken as stock. It is asked for because a raid on a lawful Imperial works is the one thing that would bring the cohorts back, and House Dres would rather protect sixty than lose the province.

rewards.name: why the salt factor wants the clause
deep water at four times the rate
what a raid on a lawful works would cost House Dres

quests.notes: Act IV voice 8 of 8. The only voice with no rank route, because there is no joining House Dres and the corpus forbids inventing one; a player with no standing anywhere reaches it exactly as easily as a player with all of it.
